about:
Watson Furniture traces its roots to 1966 when South African-born cabinetmaker and metalworker Grahame Watson opened a small workshop on Bainbridge Island, Washington. The company relocated to a 34-acre manufacturing campus in nearby Poulsbo and has remained family-owned since 2010, when Clif and Kathy McKenzie assumed majority ownership after a 1989 partnership with Bill Haggerty and Daniel Warn. Today the business is led by Chairman Clif McKenzie, President CK McKenzie, and Board Member Kathy McKenzie.

The company designs and manufactures furniture for two primary segments: modern office environments (desks, tables, systems, and storage) and mission-critical consoles for 24/7 control rooms and emergency communications centers. Production processes include a PFAS-free, heat-cured electrostatically applied coating, polypropylene edge banding as a PVC-free standard, and thermally fused low-pressure laminate fabrication. The Poulsbo facility handles all fabrication, finishing, and assembly in-house.

Customers include corporate offices, government agencies, and public-safety organizations that require durable, purpose-built furniture for high-stakes, round-the-clock operations. The firm’s pivot to mission-critical work began in 1986 when a local emergency communications center commissioned custom consoles, establishing a specialization that now runs alongside its commercial office line.

Watson emphasizes that “the way something gets made, and who makes it, matters.” Its guiding principles—Design, Craft, Partnership—are backed by a commitment to environmental accountability, evidenced by SCS Indoor Advantage Gold certification, and a promise that standard finishes ship the next business day. The company positions itself as fiercely independent, rooted in its community, and focused on integrity over shortcuts.
